title: Grateful Dead Live at Academy of Music on 1972-03-27
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> Samplitude Professional v11.2.1 -> FLAC/48k
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Apogee AD500 -> Dat (48k)

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard capture of a high‑energy Pigpen‑fronted show with a scorching Bertha opener and standout China > Rider, all delivered in crystal‑clear recording.
ai_review.review: The performance is praised for its fire‑cracker opening on “Bertha,” fierce Pigpen vocals, tight harmonies and several killer moments – especially the China > Rider sequence and the two‑soul medley.  The soundboard source is described as a “gem” with crisp, balanced audio that lets every instrument shine, making the show highly listenable despite one minor complaint about an omitted tune.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers uniformly rate the set very high (mostly 5‑star) and highlight strong musical moments; the soundboard recording is noted as clear and excellent, yielding a combined rating well above average.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, balanced mix with no reported drop‑outs or major flaws; listeners call it another gem and note the band banter is audible but not intrusive.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set launches with a hot “Bertha” and stays tight, while the second set feels like an extension of the first – a steady stream of classics and Pigpen‑driven jams without over‑extending into long improvisations.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Keeps lyrics together despite occasional slips; adds extra twang on Black Throated; backing vocals praised.
band_member_comments.Phil: Prominent backing vocals on China > Rider; fans note the “Let Phil sing” moment and his vocal contributions throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Delivers mellow ballads, especially a favored version of “Looks Like Rain”; overall solid rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano interjections are highlighted; Donna Jean’s southern‑roots vocal style is praised on several numbers.
band_member_comments.Drums: Listeners hear Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming (question about squeaky spring sound) and anticipate a juicy drum solo in “Good Lovin’.”
